Without it Node parsed each source file as CommonJS, failed, and
reparsed it as ESM, emitting MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON every time.
A warning that always fires is a warning nobody reads, and this one
sat above every test result in the log.
It does not change the build. The compiler emits CommonJS because
tsconfig.base.json sets module: commonjs, and moduleResolution: node
does not read this field at all. dist/ keeps its own package.json
boundary at the package root, so the compiled output is still
CommonJS and the API still loads it with require(). Neither tsc nor
nest copies this file into dist.
